Konstantinos "Kostas" Papanikolaou is a Greek professional basketball player.
Konstantinos "Kostas" Papanikolaou has the nickname "Air Pap".
Kostas Papanikolaou was born on 31 July 1990.
Papanikolaou plays as a small forward.
Papanikolaou is considered among the best defensive players in European basketball.
Papanikolaou won back-to-back EuroLeague championships with Olympiacos in 2012 and 2013.
Papanikolaou was the EuroLeague Finals Top Scorer in 2012.
Papanikolaou won the EuroLeague Rising Star award in 2013.
Papanikolaou reached another two finals with Olympiacos in 2017 and 2023.
Papanikolaou is the first player in EuroLeague history to record 2.000 points, 1.000 rebounds, 400 assists, 300 three-pointers made, 200 steals, and 100 blocks.
Since early in his career, Papanikolaou has been a regular member of the senior Hellenic national team.
Papanikolaou began playing basketball with the youth teams of Proteas Grevenon and Aris.
Papanikolaou made his pro debut in the Greek League, with Aris, during the 2008–09 season.
Papanikolaou was named the MVP of the Greek Youth All-Star Game in 2009.
Papanikolaou was named the Greek League's Best Young Player in 2009.
On 14 September 2009, Papanikolaou signed a five-year, €1.3 million net income deal with Olympiacos.
Olympiacos paid a €950,000 buyout fee to Aris to secure Papanikolaou's player rights.
Papanikolaou's contract with Olympiacos had an NBA buyout clause worth €1 million.
With Olympiacos, Papanikolaou won the EuroLeague and Greek League championships in 2012.
Papanikolaou was voted the EuroLeague Rising Star for the EuroLeague 2012–13 season.
With Olympiacos, Papanikolaou also won the 2012–13 season EuroLeague championship.
On 20 July 2013, Papanikolaou signed a four-year deal with FC Barcelona.
Barcelona bought Papanikolaou out of his contract with Olympiacos for €1.5 million.
Papanikolaou's contract with Barcelona was worth €5.5 million net income during the first three years (the 4th optional year would be at an additional salary).
The contract included NBA buyout clauses in the amounts of €1.1 million for 2014 and €750,000 for 2015.
Barcelona won the 2013–14 Spanish Liga ACB championship.
On 28 June 2012, Papanikolaou was selected with the 48th overall pick in the 2012 NBA draft by the New York Knicks.
Papanikolaou's draft rights were acquired by the Portland Trail Blazers via a trade that sent Raymond Felton to the Knicks.
On 16 July 2012, Papanikolaou's draft rights were acquired by the Houston Rockets via a trade that sent Thomas Robinson to the Trail Blazers.
On 23 September 2014, Papanikolaou signed with the Houston Rockets.
On 13 February 2015, Papanikolaou took part in the Rising Stars Challenge of the NBA All-Star Game.
The Rockets decided to pick up his team option for the 2015–16 season despite an injury-plagued rookie season where he averaged 4.2 points and 2.7 rebounds per game while coming off the bench.

On 20 July 2015, Papanikolaou was traded to the Denver Nuggets along with Joey Dorsey, Nick Johnson, Pablo Prigioni, a 2016 first-round draft pick, and cash considerations in exchange for Ty Lawson and a 2017 second-round draft pick.
On 25 September 2015, Papanikolaou was waived by the Denver Nuggets.
Papanikolaou re-signed with the Denver Nuggets on November 5, 2015.
Papanikolaou made his debut for the Denver Nuggets that night.
Papanikolaou was waived again by the Denver Nuggets on 7 January 2016 before his salary became fully guaranteed.
On 20 January 2016, Papanikolaou signed a two-and-a-half-year deal with Olympiacos, returning to the club for a second stint.
Papanikolaou and Olympiacos officially agreed on a new three-year contract extension on 5 July 2018.
Papanikolaou signed another three-year extension on 22 September 2020.
On July 6, 2023, Papanikolaou renewed his contract with the Greek club through 2026.

As a member of the junior national basketball teams of Greece, Papanikolaou won the silver medal at the 2007 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship and the gold medal at the 2008 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship.
Papanikolaou also won the silver medal at the 2009 FIBA Under-19 World Cup.
Papanikolaou won the gold medal at the 2009 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship and was named to the All-Tournament Team and MVP award.
Papanikolaou then won the silver medal at the 2010 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship with Greece's junior national team, where he was also named to the All-Tournament Team.
Papanikolaou made his debut with the senior men's Greek national basketball team in August 2009.

With Greece's senior national team, Papanikolaou played at EuroBasket 2011, the 2012 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament, the EuroBasket 2013, the 2014 FIBA World Cup, the EuroBasket 2015, the EuroBasket 2017, the 2019 FIBA World Cup, and the EuroBasket 2022.
Papanikolaou has appeared in 134 games for the senior national side and has scored a total of 842 points.
Papanikolaou is an off-ball player with speed and size who can play positions 2-4 comfortably.
Papanikolaou is an effective shooter from three-point range and loves to attack close-outs and finish strong at the rim.
On the other side of the ball, Papanikolaou is a great defender due to his long legs and elusive abilities.
In the 2017 Greek League, Papanikolaou was named the Best Defender.
Papanikolaou also won the same honor in the Spanish ACB League in the 2014 season.
Papanikolaou has been recognized as a leader, captaining Olympiacos to the Euroleague Championship Game in 2023.
